name: Oxybutynin topical gel (OG05009)
question: Does once-daily oxybutynin chloride topical gel reduce urge incontinence episodes more than placebo gel in adults with overactive bladder?

design.population: Adults with urgency-predominant urinary incontinence and overactive bladder, including 704 women among 789 randomized participants, had a mean age of 59 years.
design.locator: PubMed abstract, Materials and Methods and Results; ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00350636, Study Design

verdictNote: Daily urge incontinence episodes declined more with oxybutynin gel at 12 weeks.
takeaway: Once-daily oxybutynin chloride 10% topical gel reduced daily urge incontinence episodes more than placebo gel over 12 weeks in adults with urgency-predominant incontinence (mean change −3.0 versus −2.5 episodes/day; P < 0.0001).

reports.label: 12-week primary report
reports.citation: Staskin DR, Dmochowski RR, Sand PK, et al. "Efficacy and safety of oxybutynin chloride topical gel for overactive bladder: a randomized, double-blind, placebo controlled, multicenter study." *J Urol.* 2009;181(4):1764-1772. doi:10.1016/j.juro.2008.11.125

results.measure: Mean change from baseline in daily urge incontinence episodes at 12 weeks
results.note: Three-day urinary diaries; ANCOVA with last observation carried forward; no adjusted between-group difference was given in the abstract.
results.locator: PubMed abstract, Materials and Methods and Results

results.measure: Mean change from baseline in daily urinary frequency at 12 weeks
Mean change from baseline in voided volume at 12 weeks

harms.label: Serious treatment-related adverse events
harms.note: The abstract states that none occurred, without arm-specific event counts.

delivery.label: Treatment regimen
delivery.value: 1 g of 10% oxybutynin chloride topical gel or matching placebo once daily for 12 weeks.
